channel.description: Latest articles from The Honolulu Star-Advertiser (staradvertiser.com)

item.title: U.S. beat Canada in overtime thriller to end ‘golden drought’ in ice hockey
item.description: MILAN >> The United States ended a nearly half-century wait for Olympic men’s ice hockey gold with a 2-1 overtime victory against Canada in a thrilling final on Sunday, with Jack Hughes delivering their third title and first since 1980 with the winning shot.

item.title: Armed man killed trying to enter Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort
item.description: WASHINGTON >> U.S. Secret Service and local police shot and killed a man armed with a shotgun early on Sunday after he breached a secure perimeter at President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort in Palm Beach, Fla., law enforcement officials said.

item.title: U.S. reverses course to keep TSA PreCheck program operational
item.description: WASHINGTON >> The Trump administration reversed course on Sunday on the program that allows millions of airline travelers to get expedited security screening, saying it will remain operational, hours after it said the program would be temporarily suspended amid a shutdown of much of the agency.

item.title: High surf warning, advisories in effect for Hawaiian Islands
Reports: U.K. protection officers instructed to guard 2010 Epstein dinner party
item.description: LONDON >> London police officers assigned to King Charles’ younger brother Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor were instructed to provide security for a dinner party at Jeffrey Epstein’s residence in New York in 2010, British media reported on Sunday.

item.title: Police officer killed, 24 people wounded in bomb explosions in Ukraine’s Lviv
item.description: KYIV >> One police officer was killed and 24 people were wounded after several explosive devices detonated at midnight in Lviv, in western Ukraine, the National Police said on Sunday, in an attack President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed on Russia.

item.title: New York, other states under state of emergency amid blizzard warning
item.description: NEW YORK >> New York, New Jersey, Connecticut and Massachusetts governors issued state of emergency orders and a halt to non-essential travel as a major storm was expected to bring up to 24 inches of snow and strong winds to the region.

item.title: Hundreds protest in Verona ahead of Olympics closing ceremony
item.description: VERONA, Italy >> Hundreds of people marched through the streets of Verona a few hours before the Olympics closing ceremony to protest against housing costs and environmental concerns linked to the Winter Games.

item.title: Wichita State sweeps Rainbows
item.description: The Wichita State baseball team swept a doubleheader against Hawaii on Sunday, winning 13-3 and 7-1 at Les Murakami Stadium.

item.title: OHA to study feasibility of Native Hawaiian cultural center
item.description: The Office of Hawaiian Affairs announced today that it selected AEA Consulting to conduct a feasibility study for a proposed Native Hawaiian Cultural Center in Kaka‘ako Makai, launching what officials describe as a community-driven planning process for the long-discussed project.
